title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 19, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: pydantic/pydantic-ai is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: pydantic/pydantic-ai leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: pydantic/pydantic-ai — 14 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 4.2 above its current daily pace, with 3 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 108 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 564 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Test whether resume replays work or starts it again
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code now refuses a stored workflow resume when its journal is missing and makes eligible interrupted runs visible on a later interactive or ACP start.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The journal loader distinguishes absence from an empty replay. A separate checkpoint records a registered attempt, and a later eligible process can turn it into failed history with an interruption explanation. Resumption remains explicit.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A supervisor needs to distinguish saved results that can be replayed from agent calls that would execute again under a familiar run identifier.

actions.label: Exercise a disposable two-step restart
actions.instruction: On a build containing both changes, interrupt a harmless two-step workflow after the first recorded result. Restart interactively and inspect interrupted history, then explicitly resume and count live steps. In a separate disposable case remove the journal and confirm refusal. Keep external side effects out of this test.
actions.effort: 20–30 minutes with an existing test installation

receipts.title: Refuse missing-journal resume
receipts.supports: The loader distinguishes missing and unreadable journals; the runner refuses them before dispatch with storage configured.

receipts.title: Discover interrupted workflow runs
receipts.supports: Checkpoints let later interactive or ACP startup surface eligible interrupted attempts as failed history.

confidence.basis: The merged runner, journal and checkpoint implementation agree with the added regression cases and public PR descriptions.

dailyInsight.limitation: No live process-kill reproduction or released-package mapping was performed. Best-effort persistence, legacy empty journals and headless discovery limits prevent a blanket recovery guarantee.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call if the installed implementation accepts a missing stored journal and dispatches agents, or a later patch changes the explicit-resume and ownership rules.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A released version and reproducible restart test showing which results replay and which agent calls execute again.
